segments.title: 900年孤独与旧书摊的震惊发现
segments.original: This song is almost 900 years old. It was written by Comtessa de Dia, a poet and composer from medieval southern France. It is the only surviving melody written by a woman from that entire tradition. So let me start with the question: who decides which voices survive? I never really thought about that until a few years ago, when I was working in a second-hand book market in London, and I found an encyclopedia that listed 6,000 women composers in the history of music. I could not believe it because at that time I think I could name five. But as soon as I started looking into their names and listening to this incredible music, I kid you not, I would not shut up. Well I haven't shut up. I'm here. And I just am sharing this music with everybody all the time. In fact, please allow me.
segments.translation: 这首歌已有将近 900 年的历史了。它是由中世纪法国南部的诗人兼作曲家迪亚伯爵夫人所作。这是那个时代完整传统中，由女性谱写的唯一流传至今的旋律。那么，请允许我以这样一个问题开始：究竟是谁在决定，哪些声音能够流传下来？直到几年前，我从未真正思考过这个问题。当时我在伦敦的一家二手旧书市场工作，偶然发现了一本百科全书，里面列出了音乐史上 6,000 位女性作曲家。我简直不敢相信，因为在那个时候，我觉得自己顶多只能说出 5 个名字。但当我开始查阅她们的名字、聆听这些令人震撼的音乐时——没骗你，我根本停不下来。好吧，到现在我也没停过，我就站在这里。我一直在不停地与所有人分享这些音乐。事实上，请允许我放一段给大家听。

segments.title: 现场乐曲赏析 (Music Interlude)
segments.original: (Music: Classical strings mixed with Afro-American romantic dance rhythms playing on stage...)
segments.translation: （现场播放音乐片段：古典弦乐融合非裔美国人浪漫舞蹈节拍……）

segments.title: 台下互动与丈夫的日常调侃
segments.original: I mean, can you believe that? Did you hear all the classical strings? The Afro-American dances mixed with the romantic music? Well welcome to my husband's life in 2018. (Laughter)
segments.translation: 我是说，你们能相信吗？你们听到那些古典弦乐了吗？融合了浪漫主义音乐的非裔美国人舞蹈节奏？好吧，欢迎体验我丈夫在 2018 年的生活状态。（笑声）

segments.title: 铁路工程师丈夫的幽默自嘲
segments.original: Now, my husband, he's a railway engineer, which means he's now the railway engineer who knows the most about women composers in the whole world. (Laughter) I know, it's not a very competitive field, but still. (Laughter)
segments.translation: 我丈夫是个铁路工程师，这意味着他现在成了全世界上最了解女性作曲家的铁路工程师。（笑声）我知道，这并不是一个竞争多么激烈的领域，但这依然很厉害。（笑声）

segments.title: 从早餐碎碎念到创立 18,000 人全球基金会
segments.original: So one day he said to me, 'Look, it's very nice that you're playing this music by these women at breakfast for like, I don't know, a year now. But you do understand that nothing is going to happen if you just tell me. I'm an engineer. So are you going to do something or what?' And I was like, 'Fair enough.' So I did. I made a list of these incredible women. I put it online, and within months, women from all over the world started writing to me and they said, 'Thank you so much for what you're doing. I'm a composer. Could you please add me to your list?' And I tell you, this list continues to grow. It is now a foundation, and we are now uncovering over 18,000 women composers in the history of music. (Applause)
segments.translation: 于是有一天他对我说：‘听着，你每天吃早餐时放这些女性作曲家的音乐，都放了大概一年了，这确实挺好。但你应该明白，只跟我讲，这个世界不会发生任何改变。我是个工程师。所以你到底打不打算做点什么？’ 我当时心想：‘说得在理。’ 于是我行动了。我为这些杰出的女性整理了一份清单发布到网上。几个月之内，全世界的女性开始给我写信：‘太感谢你的付出了。我也是一名作曲家，能把我也加进你的名单吗？’ 我告诉大家，这份名单还在不断壮大。它现在已经变成了一个基金会，我们已经在音乐史上发掘出了超过 18,000 位女性作曲家。（掌声）

segments.title: 职业音乐人的认知反思与 90% 悬殊差距
segments.original: Now this story makes absolutely no sense. I'm a professional musician. How is it possible that I spent my life training and performing without hearing about thousands of women who wrote beautiful music? Well when I started doing my own research, and I came across the data, then it became clear because, it turns out, that nearly 90 percent of the music we hear across genres is written by men. That's a very big gap. Can you imagine all the amazing music we've been all missing all this time? But also that AI is now learning from that same silence. On one platform only, more than 50,000 AI-generated tracks are added every single day. The systems can only learn from the data available to them, but right now that data is missing. Half of humanity's creativity. Now I believe musicians should be writing music, not machines. (Applause)
segments.translation: 仔细想想，这整件事根本毫无逻辑。我是一名受过专业训练的职业音乐人。我怎么可能花了一辈子在训练和演出，却从未听说过成千上万谱写出绝美旋律的女性？当我开始自己动手调研并看到真实数据时，一切真相大白：事实证明，我们在所有流派中听到的音乐里，近 90% 都是由男性创作的。这是个巨大的鸿沟。你能想象我们一直以来错过了多少动人心魄的音乐吗？更可怕的是，人工智能现在正在从这种同样的历史沉默中吸收养分。仅在某一个平台上，每天就会上传超过 50,000 首由 AI 生成的音轨。AI 系统只能从现存可用数据中学习，但眼下这些数据是残缺的——人类一半的创造力在其中缺席了。我坚信，写音乐的应该是音乐家，而不是机器。（掌声）

segments.title: 艺术伦理：未经许可与报酬使用创作是错误的
segments.original: There are millions of talented people who can do that. Writing music fills our soul ... as humans. And to generate music from artists' work without their consent or proper remuneration is wrong. (Applause and cheers)
segments.translation: 世界上有数以百万计才华横溢的人能够创作音乐。创作音乐滋养着我们作为人类的灵魂。而未经艺术家同意、不给予合理报酬，就用他们的作品来生成音乐，这是不道德的。（掌声与欢呼）

segments.title: 正视技术浪潮：通过录制让尘封作品重现光芒
segments.original: But the technology is here to stay. So let's make sure all voices are heard, right? So how do we do that? It's actually quite easy. We must record the missing voices -- the historical ones, but also the current ones who are not represented. Because a recording makes this music searchable, teachable, and part of the systems shaping what the world will hear next. It brings this music to classrooms, to radio stations, to streaming platforms so everybody in this room can play and share it.
segments.translation: 然而技术浪潮不可阻挡。所以我们必须确保所有的声音都能被听见，对吗？那我们该怎么做？其实非常简单。我们必须把那些缺失的声音录制下来——包括历史上的，也包括当下未被充分代表的声音。因为录音让这些音乐变得可检索、可教学，并成为塑造未来世界听觉系统的一部分。它能把这些作品带入教室、电台和流媒体平台，让在场的每个人都能演奏与分享。

segments.title: 向科技巨头的郑重倡议：被听见的才是被铭记的
segments.original: So here's my invitation. What if every tech company making AI music and anyone profiting from it would invest in making our musical catalog more complete? Can you imagine? What gets heard is chosen, and those choices will shape what the future will remember. So who decides which voices survive? Now more than ever, we do.
segments.translation: 因此，这是我的倡议：如果每家研发 AI 音乐的科技公司以及从中获利的各方，都能投资去完善我们的音乐馆藏，那会怎样？你能想象吗？能被听到的声音是经过选择的，而那些选择将决定未来会记住什么。那么，究竟是谁在决定哪些声音能够流传？比以往任何时候都更确定的是：决定权在我们手里。

segments.title: 集中营里埋在工具棚下的摇篮曲《Wiegala》
segments.original: And I want to leave you all with one woman's story. Ilse Weber was a poet, a singer who was imprisoned in the ghetto of Theresienstadt during World War II with her family. As she was there, she didn't write symphonies, but she wrote songs to entertain the elderly and the children. That's the power of music. And that was the gift of one woman. She and her son sadly died in Auschwitz, but her husband buried her manuscripts under a tool shed, and because of that, a few of her songs survived. This one is a lullaby. It's called 'Wiegala'.
segments.translation: 最后，我想给大家留下一个女性的故事。伊尔丝·韦伯（Ilse Weber）是一位诗人和歌唱家，二战期间她与家人一起被囚禁在特雷津集中营隔离区。在那里，她没有创作交响乐，而是写歌来抚慰老人和孩子们。这就是音乐的力量，也是一个普通女性的奉献。遗憾的是，她和儿子最终在奥斯威辛遇难，但她的丈夫把她的乐谱手稿埋在了一个工具棚下面，正因如此，她的几首歌才得以留存人世。这首是一首摇篮曲，叫作《Wiegala》。

segments.title: 历史沉默的震撼收尾与全场掌声
segments.original: (Singing 'Wiegala'...) (Song stops abruptly) [If you can't hear this part, perhaps history never recorded it.] Artificial intelligence is learning. Let's teach it to remember the sounds of all of us. Thank you. (Applause)
segments.translation: （现场演唱摇篮曲《Wiegala》……）（歌声戛然而止）[如果你听不到这一部分，也许是因为历史从未将它记录下来。] 人工智能正在学习。让我们教会它去铭记我们所有人的声音。谢谢大家。（全场热烈掌声）

segments.title: 芦屋市的年轻面孔与竞选奇迹
segments.original: TED Fellow Ryosuke Takashima made international headlines as the youngest-ever mayor in Japan's history. But when you ask him about the label, he waves it away with a warm, humble smile.
segments.translation: TED Fellow 高岛崚辅作为日本宪政史上最年轻的市长登上了全球各大媒体头条。但当你向他提及这个耀眼的年轻标签时，他总是带着温和谦逊的微笑摆摆手。

segments.title: 倾听的力量：走进老年人与中学生的日常对话
segments.original: His core philosophy of governance is refreshingly simple: don't start with rigid policy decrees; start by sitting down and listening to as many voices as possible.
segments.translation: 他的治理核心哲学质朴而深刻：不要从冷冰冰的教条政策开始；相反，坐下来，去倾听尽可能多元真实的声音——从退休长者到中学生。

segments.title: 打破官僚壁垒：公民如何成为自己家园的共创者
segments.original: In this inspiring conversation with Lily James Olds, Ryosuke explains why youth is not an obstacle in public service, but a superpower that allows him to ask honest questions and advocate for systemic renewal.
segments.translation: 在与 Lily James Olds 的深度对话中，高岛崚辅阐明了为什么在公共事务中年轻不是障碍，而是一项超能力：它让你能够卸下包袱提出真诚的质询，推动系统性的破局更新。

segments.title: 重塑公共信任：在多极动荡世界中的长情陪伴
segments.original: True community resilience is never engineered from the top down; it is nurtured hand in hand, conversation by conversation, until every citizen feels truly seen and valued.
segments.translation: 真正的社区复原力绝非自上而下行政规划的产物；它是一场手拉手、面对面的真诚对话，直到每一位普通市民都切实感受到自己被倾听、被尊重。

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche: OK, can you hear me? Audience: Yes. YMR: Yes? Great. That is the meditation. So, finished. My TED Talk is finished. (Laughter and applause) Of course, I'm just kidding. (Laughter) So the more, when you try to stop thinking what happens, you will think more. So we will do a small experiment, OK? Now, please don't think about pizza. (Laughter) No pizza. No pizza. What happened? Did you think about pizza or not? Yes, raise your hand. (Laughter) I know. (Laughter) Actually, we don't need to stop thinking.
segments.translation: 但很多人却觉得很难。为什么呢？因为关于冥想通常有两个误区。第一个误区是很多人认为冥想意味着“什么都不想、停止思考、高度专注”。“嘘！我在冥想，保持安静！”（笑声）但是，当你越试图停止思考时，会发生什么？你会想得更多。我们来做个小实验好吗？现在，请大家绝对不要去想披萨。（笑声）不要想披萨，不要想披萨。结果怎样？你想没想披萨？想了的举手。（笑声）我就知道。（笑声）事实上，我们根本不需要停止思考。

segments.title: 误区二与童年焦虑：暴风雨与影子
segments.original: We just need to connect with awareness. And another misunderstanding about meditation is what we call 'blissing out.' Looking for peace, calm, joy, relax. (Laughter) The more you look for relax, then peace, calm, joy, relax run away. So ... Let me share [with] you my own experience. When I was young, I had panic attacks. Although I was born right in the middle of the Himalayan mountains, the area, the village, wonderful, but panic followed me like a shadow. And I have so much fear [of] strangers, I cannot go out and meet people. And lot of storms in the Himalayan mountains, thunderstorm, snowstorm. These storms drive me crazy. And when I was nine years old, I asked my father to teach me meditation.
segments.translation: 我们只需要与自己的“觉知”建立连接。而关于冥想的另一个误区就是所谓的“沉溺极乐”——拼命追求平和、平静、喜悦与放松。（笑声）你越是刻意追求放松，平和、平静、喜悦和放松反而跑得越快。那么……让我分享一下我自己的亲身经历。小时候，我饱受惊恐发作（panic attacks）的折磨。虽然我出生在喜马拉雅山脉腹地，村庄美轮美奂，但恐慌却像影子一样如影随形。我对陌生人极度恐惧，不敢出门见人。喜马拉雅山脉多暴风雨，雷暴、暴风雪……这些风暴简直要把我逼疯。九岁那年，我请求父亲教我冥想。

segments.title: 父亲的开示：天空与山中暴风雨
segments.original: Luckily, he was a great meditation teacher. And the first thing what he said is, "Don't try to fight with the panic. Don't try to get rid of panic." "And actually," he said, "you don't have to." Why? Awareness is like sky in the mountain, and the panic is like storm in the mountain, like cloud. And no matter how strong a storm is, it doesn't change the nature of sky. So sky is always present, pure, calm. Similarly, our fundamental quality of mind, awareness is always present, pure, calm. But the problem is we don't know how to connect with awareness, what we see, only a thought, emotion, that's all. So he said, there are three steps of practice to connect with awareness. The first one, we have to use an object.
segments.translation: 幸运的是，他是一位伟大的禅修导师。他对我说的一句话就是：“不要试图去和恐慌对抗，不要试图摆脱恐慌。”“而且事实上，”他说，“你根本没必要对抗。”为什么？因为觉知就像山中的天空，而恐慌就像山中的风暴和乌云。无论暴风雨多么狂暴，它都改变不了天空的本质。天空永远都在那里，纯净、广阔、安详。同样，我们心智的根本特质——觉知，也永远都在，纯净而平静。但问题是我们不知道如何连接觉知，我们眼里看到的只有念头和情绪。于是他说，连接觉知有三个练习步骤。第一步：借助一个外在对象。

segments.title: 第一步：借助声音作为锚点
segments.original: Support, to connect with awareness. So this is one of my first meditation techniques that I learned from my father. So you can join and you can relax your muscles in your body. If you cannot relax, also OK, allowed. (Laughter) And close your eyes, and please listen to sound. (Ding) And when you hear the sound, through ear and mind together ... (Ding) That is the meditation. And let panic come and go. Let pizza come and go. (Ding) And maybe two pizzas, three pizzas, ten pizzas. As long as you remember the sound, you can have pizza. (Ding)
segments.translation: 也就是借助一个支撑物来连接觉知。这是我从父亲那里学到的最早的冥想方法之一。大家现在可以和我一起做：放松全身肌肉；如果你放松不下来，也没关系，允许自己不放松。（笑声）闭上双眼，请倾听声音。（磬声响起）当你用耳朵和心灵一同聆听这声音时……（磬声）这就是冥想。任凭恐慌来来去去，任凭披萨念头来来去去。（磬声）就算脑子里出现两张披萨、三张披萨、十张披萨也无妨，只要你还记得听声音，随便你想多少披萨都行。（磬声）

segments.title: 懒惰男孩与三年闭关的开端
segments.original: (Ding) (Ding) OK, how was it? Did you hear the sound? Yes, raise your hand. Great. That is the meditation. Very easy. Just hear, that's all. You don't have to do anything. So if panic comes, let panic come and go, don't care. Just listen to sound. Monkey mind comes blah, blah, blah. Let it come and go, just listen to sound. So I did that. But I had a big problem. The problem is lazy. (Laughter) I'm lazy boy, I love the idea of meditation, but I don't like the practice of meditation. So on and off like that for five years. When I was 13 years old in India, there's traditional three-year retreat going to start. I thought I should join this because it's good for my laziness.
segments.translation: （磬声）好了，感觉如何？你们听到声音了吗？听到的请举手。太棒了。这就是冥想。非常简单，仅仅是去听，仅此而已，你不需要做任何额外的事。如果恐慌出现，任它来来去去，不用在意，只要听声音；“心猿”杂念开始碎碎念，任它来去，专心听声音。我就照着练习。但我遇到了一个大问题：我很懒。（笑声）我是个懒男孩，我喜欢冥想的理念，但讨厌冥想的实修。就这样断断续续过了五年。13岁那年，印度有一场传统的三年闭关即将开始。我想我应该参加，因为这正好能治治我的懒病。

segments.title: 闭关困境：懒惰与恐慌成了密友
segments.original: And I join. The first month, wonderful, no lazy. Second month, lazy come back. (Laughter) Now what happened? My lazy and my panic, they two become good friends. (Laughter) The life in the retreat becomes disaster. And I thought I should leave. But I feel embarrassed to leave because I told all my childhood friends that I can do the retreat, you know. I don't want to lose my face. But if I stay, almost three years to go. Then I thought, what should I do? In the end, I decided to learn how to live with the panic. So now we have the second step what we call, actually, we can meditate everywhere, anytime with anything. So you can meditate with panic. How do you do that? Just like listen to sound, when you listen to sound, sound becomes support for your meditation. Now you're going to watch panic.
segments.translation: 于是我参加了。第一个月，感觉好极了，一点都不偷懒。第二个月，懒惰卷土重来。（笑声）结果发生了什么？我的懒惰和我的恐慌，这两个家伙居然结成了密友！（笑声）闭关生活成了一场灾难。我一度想要放弃离开，但我又觉得太丢人，因为我已经告诉了所有儿时的玩伴我能完成三年闭关，我可不想丢面子。可如果要留下来，还有将近三年时间啊！我想：我该怎么办？最终，我决定学会与恐慌共处。这就来到了第二步：事实上，我们随时随地可以用任何事物来冥想。你可以把恐慌本身当作冥想的对象。怎么做呢？就像刚才听声音一样，声音是冥想的依托，而现在，你去观察你的恐慌。

segments.title: 第二步：看见河流与剃须泡沫隐喻
segments.original: If you see the panic, great. What we call, when you see the river, you're out of the river. When you see the mountain, you're out of the montain. So now awareness becomes more than panic. More than depression, stress. Monkey mind, whatever. Let them come, let them go. So that is the first benefit and second benefit of what we call, there's a wisdom comes. So when you look at the panic, panic is not solid stone anymore. Panic becomes pieces. Sensation here, frightening image, voice, background belief. And if you take one of these away, you cannot find panic. So what I call panic becomes like shaving foam, looks like a piece of rock but inside full of bubbles. Then three, what I call this is acceptance,
segments.translation: 如果你能“看见”恐慌，那就太好了。这就叫：当你看见河流时，你已经身在河外了；当你看见大山时，你已经脱离大山了。此时，你的觉知超越了恐慌，超越了抑郁、压力和杂乱的心猿。任它们来，任它们去。这是第一重益处。第二重益处是我们所说的“智慧生起”：当你仔细端详恐慌时，它不再是一块坚不可摧的顽石，而是碎成了片片碎片——身体局部的紧绷感、恐怖的幻象、内心的低语、潜意识的信念……如果你抽走其中任何一个，你甚至都找不到恐慌在哪里。所以恐慌就像剃须泡沫，远看像一块岩石，其实里面全是泡沫。第三点则是彻底的接纳：

segments.title: 买一赠二：恐慌成了最好的老师
segments.original: like self-kind, self-love, self-compassion. You let panic come and go, that's the real acceptance, isn't it? So three in one: awareness, love and compassion, wisdom. Sometimes what I call buy one, get two free. (Laughter) Big deal, right? And all this because of panic. So now panic becomes your teacher, your best friend. So I did this practice and in the end, me and my panic become very good friends. And few weeks later, panic is gone. I miss my friend. And I finished my retreat, my retreat went very well. And after that I have been eager to share this wonderful technique with the world. So I taught meditation many places, wrote three books, become bestseller, and then students and become abbot of a few monasteries. And what happened?
segments.translation: 那就是自我善待、自我关爱、自我慈悲。你允许恐慌自如来去，这才是真正的接纳，不是吗？这就是“三合一”：觉知、爱与慈悲、以及智慧。有时我称之为“买一赠二”（笑声）。超值的交易对吧？而这一切都是恐慌赋予你的。现在，恐慌成了你的导师，成了你最要好的朋友。我坚持这样修习，最终我和我的恐慌成了莫逆之交。几周后，恐慌彻底消失了——我甚至开始想念我的老朋友。我圆满完成了三年闭关，状态极佳。此后我热切地想把这套法门分享给全世界。我在世界各地传道，写了三本书成为畅销书作家，门徒众多，并成为几座寺院的住持。然而紧接着又发生了什么呢？

segments.title: 游方行脚：流落街头与濒死之境
segments.original: Kind of new ego emerged within me. I thought, oh, I have to watch out, this so. Then I decided to do something very special, what we call wandering retreat. Meaning you leave everything behind, go on the street with nothing. So I decided to do that. In 2011, I left my monastery, my students, my wonderful cozy bed. Everything, and got on street with only a few thousand Indian rupees, and that finished within a few weeks. Now I have to beg for food. And I got food poisoning. Vomiting, diarrhea. I'm alone on the street, now I'm going to die. Then I thought, what should I do? So now we have the third step, what we call open awareness meditation. Awareness, be with itself. Sky, be with itself.
segments.translation: 一种新的“自我膨胀（ego）”在内心悄然滋生。我想：哦，我必须警惕了。于是我决定做一件非同寻常的事——我们称之为“游方苦修（wandering retreat）”。这意味着抛弃一切，身无分文走上街头。2011年，我毅然离开寺院、弟子和我那张温暖舒适的大床，孑然一身走上街头，身上只有几千印度卢比，几周内就花光了。我不得不沿街乞讨。接着我食物中毒，上吐下泻，独自一人瘫倒在街头，觉得自己快要死了。那时我想：我该怎么办？这就带出了第三步：所谓“开放觉知冥想（open awareness meditation）”。让觉知安住于觉知自身，如浩瀚长空与自身共处。

segments.title: 第三步：开放觉知与万物一体
segments.original: Now, no need to have support. Just be awareness itself. I did that practice. Then what happened? My body become decayed, I cannot see, I cannot hear. But my mind becomes so present, beyond free. And I was in that state for a few hours. Luckily, I didn't die, I come back. So when I come back, the street becomes like my home. When I look at a tree, tree becomes like tree of love. And the wind blows to my face become a joyful experience. And the rest of my retreat went very well. I learned a lot from my retreat. So I like to share this open awareness meditation, but it is very difficult to explain. But I want to do something drama. And this is what I learned from my father. So what we call, this mala is the crazy monkey mind,
segments.translation: 此时此刻，不再需要任何外在的依靠或支撑，仅仅安住于觉知本身。我进行了这样的禅修。随后发生了什么？我的肉体仿佛衰竭瓦解，我看不见也听不清，但我的意识却变得前所未有的临在，超越了一切束缚与自由。我沉浸在那样的境界中数个小时。幸运的是，我没有死，我缓了过来。当我重返人世时，街头变成了我的家园；当我望向一棵树，那棵树化作了充满慈爱的生命；拂过面颊的微风，都成了一种纯然喜悦的体验。我此后的苦修之旅一切顺利，我从中领悟良多。我很想向大家分享这种开放觉知，但它确实很难用言语解释。不过我想用一种戏剧化的方式演示，这也是我从父亲那里学来的。我们手中的念珠就好比纷乱的心猿……

segments.title: 结语：无需刻意冥想，纯然临在
segments.original: blah, blah, blah, yada yada. And the open awareness meditation means you don't have to do anything. Just be. That's all, and you don't need to meditate. The sense of presence, being, but not loss. Be free. Be present. Thank you very much.
segments.translation: ……无论心猿如何喋喋不休，开放觉知意味着你什么都不用做，只是“安住（Just be）”。仅此而已，你甚至不需要刻意去冥想。那种当下的临在感，那种纯然的存在，而没有迷失。保持自由，安住当下。非常感谢大家。

title: The 60 seconds that make or break a conversation
chineseTitle: 决定职场沟通成败的关键 60 秒：3 步框架让你一开口就讲中要点
speaker: Chris Fenning
speakerTitle: 全球资深沟通教练 · 畅销书作者
rawAdTrimmed: 已剔除片头片尾赞助广告
quote: Frame the conversation, state the purpose, and make the ask in sixty seconds.
quoteTranslation: 在最初的六十秒内搭好背景、表明目的并提出具体诉求。

segments.title: 漫长铺垫的职场噩梦：沟通效率的隐形杀手
segments.original: What's your point? In busy workplaces, rambling context and endless backstory exhaust listeners long before the actual problem is ever stated.
segments.translation: 你到底想说什么？在节奏紧凑的职场中，冗长的背景铺垫和无边无际的来龙去脉，往往在实质性问题被抛出之前就早已耗尽了倾听者的耐心。

segments.title: 黄金 60 秒法则：为什么第一分钟决定一切
segments.original: Communication expert Chris Fenning demonstrates that the outcome of almost any meeting or pitch is effectively determined during the opening sixty seconds.
segments.translation: 沟通专家克里斯·芬宁指出，几乎任何职场会议或方案汇报的最终走向与成败，在开场的最初 60 秒内就已经被注定了。

segments.title: 三步破局框架：背景、目的与精准诉求
segments.original: Here is the blueprint: first, name the topic in one sentence; second, state why this meeting matters today; third, clarify exactly what you need from the other person.
segments.translation: 这套破局三步法如下：第一，用一句话定义核心主题；第二，明确为何今天必须讨论此事；第三，清晰指出你需要对方作出什么决定或支持。

segments.title: 尊重他人时间：高阶职业素养的终极体现
segments.original: When you master the discipline of brevity, you show profound respect for your colleagues' attention, and suddenly everyone wants to listen to you.
segments.translation: 当你掌握了言简意赅的表达素养，你便向同事展示出了对他人注意力的极高尊重，而此时，每个人都会由衷地渴望聆听你的想法。

spoken.meaning: 决定成败 / 关键转折点
spoken.quote: The first sixty seconds can make or break a workplace conversation.
spoken.pronunciation: make or break 是口语经典搭配，make 的 /k/ 与 or 自然连读。

spoken.meaning: 你到底想表达什么核心论点？
spoken.quote: How often have you listened to someone speak and secretly thought: what is your point?
spoken.pronunciation: point 尾音 /t/ 干净利落，语气直接。

grammar.name: 祈使句排比与行动框架
grammar.quote: Frame the context, state your core intention, and specify the exact ask.
grammar.explanation: 通过三个动作动词引导的并列祈使句，建立清晰易记的行动法则。

vocab.detail: 指在极短时间内向决策层传达最高密度高价值信息的能力。
商务沟通中指不含糊、对方能够立即明确回答或采取行动的请求。

slug: mark-whittle-this is what the birth of the
title: This is what the birth of the universe sounded like
chineseTitle: 倾听宇宙大爆炸的初啼：天文学家带你聆听宇宙诞生的声音
speaker: Mark Whittle
speakerTitle: 弗吉尼亚大学天体物理学教授
rawAdTrimmed: 已剔除片头片尾赞助广告
quote: The early universe was not silent; it was filled with deep harmonic sound waves traveling through cosmic plasma.
quoteTranslation: 早期的宇宙绝非死寂一片；它充盈着在宇宙等离子体中穿行的深邃泛音与声波。

segments.title: 大爆炸之后的声音：宇宙初生的第一声啼鸣
segments.original: What sound came immediately after the Big Bang? Most of us imagine the early universe as a silent black void, but physics tells a breathtakingly different story.
segments.translation: 在大爆炸之后紧接着出现的声音究竟是什么？我们大多数人都把早期的宇宙想象为一片死寂黑暗的虚无，但天体物理学却讲述了一个截然不同、震撼人心的故事。

segments.title: 穿越百亿年：穿透等离子体的巨型声波
segments.original: Astronomer Mark Whittle takes us back to the infant cosmos, where massive sound waves pulsed through primordial gas in majestic harmonic chords.
segments.translation: 天文学家马克·惠特尔带我们穿越回百亿年前的婴儿期宇宙：在那里，巨大的声波在太初等离子体中震颤回响，交织成壮丽宏伟的泛音和弦。

segments.title: 科学与艺术的共鸣：太古声音化为现代合唱
segments.original: Collaborating with composer Caroline Shaw and artist Ander Mikalson, Whittle translated these cosmic microwave fluctuations into an awe-inspiring human choral masterpiece.
segments.translation: 惠特尔与普利策音乐奖得主卡洛琳·肖以及声音艺术家安德·米卡尔森跨界携手，将这组古老的宇宙微波涨落数据破译为一部令人叹为观止的人类合唱巨作。

segments.title: 我们体内流淌的星尘与太古和弦
segments.original: The atoms making up our vocal cords and eardrums were forged in those very vibrations. When we sing, the universe is listening to its own origin.
segments.translation: 构成我们声带与耳膜的每一个原子，皆铸就于那场古老震荡的炽热熔炉之中。当我们开口歌唱，宇宙便是在聆听自己最初的心跳。

spoken.meaning: 带我们穿越回……
spoken.quote: Astronomer Mark Whittle takes us back to the infant cosmos billions of years ago.
spoken.pronunciation: take us back 辅元连读。

spoken.meaning: 在……范围内清晰可寻
spoken.quote: These ancient acoustic pulses are still traceable across the cosmic microwave background today.
spoken.pronunciation: traceable 重音在第一音节。

grammar.name: 同位语与非限制性从句嵌套
grammar.quote: Mark Whittle takes us to the infant cosmos, where massive sound waves pulsed in patterns still visible today.
grammar.explanation: where 引导非限制性定语从句生动描摹百亿年前宇宙声波在星系中留下的壮丽痕迹。

vocab.detail: 大爆炸后早期宇宙物质尚未形成中性原子时的极端高能流体状态。
天体物理学中用于精确测量宇宙膨胀速率与暗能量性质的标准尺。
